ameSoeur.introTitle: Is this really the right person?
ameSoeur.modeSoloDesc: Is your partner your soulmate or not?
ameSoeur.modeCelibDesc: A portrait of who would suit you
ameSoeur.modeDesc: The test adapts to your situation.
ameSoeur.v_ames_d: All four pillars are there at once, and that is rare. You are yourself effortlessly with {{name}}, you agree on the things that matter and not just on tastes, you have been through something together and the bond came out stronger. And above all, you did not disappear along the way. That last part is what separates a soulmate from a beautiful story: you are not one because one of you faded out, but because two whole people hold together.
ameSoeur.v_ames_a: Do not take this for granted. What got you here are everyday reflexes, not luck: keep seeing people on your own, keep saying things early, and keep repairing quickly after arguments.
ameSoeur.v_devenir_d: The ease is there, and so is the agreement. What is missing is not quality, it is time. Nothing has come to test this bond yet: no real blow, no argument you struggle to recover from. And that is exactly where you find out whether a relationship is a shelter or a good season. You have everything you need, what you lack is the proof.
ameSoeur.v_devenir_a: Do not go looking for hardship, it will come. In the meantime, watch how you handle small irritations: the way people repair a scratch says a fair amount about how they will absorb a real blow.
ameSoeur.v_fusion_d: You get on wonderfully, the ease is real, and yet something is off: you have shrunk. Friends have drifted away, personal projects have been dropped, a day without news becomes hard to get through. A soulmate does not cost that. "Being one" is a fine phrase as long as both people still exist; when one of the two disappears, that is no longer loving fusion, it is dependence.
ameSoeur.v_fusion_a: Take back one thing, just one, that you had let go: a friend, a sport, an evening of your own. Then watch what happens. A solid relationship absorbs that without drama; if it triggers a crisis, you have just learned something important.
ameSoeur.v_route_d: You agree on the things that matter, you have supported each other through hard times, and you have each kept your own life. What is missing is the ease: with {{name}}, you still have to be careful, choose your words, play a part. That is not a failure, and it is not nothing, plenty of solid couples rest on exactly that. But what you are describing sounds more like a good team than a soulmate.
ameSoeur.v_route_a: Look at where the restraint comes from. If it is the fear of being judged, it can fall away, sometimes in a single conversation. If it is a deep disagreement you have been walking around since the start, naming it beats circling it.
ameSoeur.v_croisent_d: This is not a verdict on {{name}}, nor on you. Your answers describe a relationship where ease is missing, where deep agreement is not there, and where difficulty has not brought you closer. Two good people can simply not suit each other, and that takes nothing away from what you have lived. The useful question is not "is this my soulmate", it is "am I doing well in this relationship".
ameSoeur.v_croisent_a: Take three weeks and write down, every evening, how you feel after seeing {{name}}. Read it back cold. What you feel over time says more than any test, this one included.
ameSoeur.cv_h: You read each other the same way, and high. That is the most reliable signal in the test: when both versions of the same story match, they stand a good chance of being right.
ameSoeur.cv_ecart: Your two readings differ sharply. One of you is living this relationship more peacefully than the other, and that deserves a conversation before anything else. The lower score is not the one that is wrong.
ameSoeur.cv_m: You are describing the same relationship, with the same reservations. Nothing alarming, nothing obvious either: the bond holds, it does not yet have what makes a soulmate.
ameSoeur.cv_l: You agree, and that is precisely the problem: neither of you describes a relationship that carries them. That is useful information, and you gathered it together.
ameSoeur.q1: When you are with {{name}}, how much do you have to watch what you say?
ameSoeur.q1a: A lot. I weigh every word.
ameSoeur.q1b: Often, on certain topics I avoid.
ameSoeur.q1c: Rarely, except when the moment is tense.
ameSoeur.q1d: Never. I say what I think, as it comes.
ameSoeur.q2a: They make me uncomfortable, I scramble for something to say.
ameSoeur.q2b: They are a bit awkward, we end up filling them.
ameSoeur.q2c: They are fine most of the time.
ameSoeur.q2d: We can say nothing for an hour and it stays pleasant.
ameSoeur.q3: The version of you nobody sees, does {{name}} know it?
ameSoeur.q3a: No, and I do everything to keep them from seeing it.
ameSoeur.q3b: A little, and I am afraid of what they would think.
ameSoeur.q3d: Yes, entirely, and it changed nothing.
ameSoeur.q4: After spending time with {{name}}, how do you feel?
ameSoeur.q4a: Drained, as if after an effort.
ameSoeur.q4b: It depends a lot on the day.
ameSoeur.q4d: Recharged. It is the moment of the week I look forward to.
ameSoeur.q5: Do you ever rehearse a conversation in your head before starting it with {{name}}?
ameSoeur.q5b: Often, as soon as the subject is delicate.
ameSoeur.q5d: Never, I dive in and we will see.
ameSoeur.q6: If you got important news, good or bad, {{name}} would be:
ameSoeur.q6a: Someone I would tell later, if I remembered.
ameSoeur.q6b: One of the people I would call during the day.
ameSoeur.q7: On how to treat people, a waiter, a stranger, someone who gets it wrong, {{name}} and you:
ameSoeur.q7a: We react completely differently, and it bothers me.
ameSoeur.q7d: We have the same reflex, without ever having discussed it.
ameSoeur.q8: Money: what we spend, what we keep, what we lend.
ameSoeur.q8a: It is a recurring source of tension.
ameSoeur.q8c: We come to an agreement after talking.
ameSoeur.q8d: We see things the same way.
ameSoeur.q9: What you call a good life, ten years from now:
ameSoeur.q9a: Two plans that do not fit together.
ameSoeur.q10: Loyalty: what is acceptable and what is not.
ameSoeur.q10a: We have never discussed it, and I do not think we agree.
ameSoeur.q10b: We have discussed it, and our limits differ.
ameSoeur.q10d: We did not need to discuss it to be on the same line.
ameSoeur.q11: Faced with someone who needs help, {{name}} reacts:
ameSoeur.q11a: In a way that makes me uncomfortable.
ameSoeur.q11c: Like me, most of the time.
ameSoeur.q11d: Exactly as I would have reacted.
ameSoeur.q12a: Nothing in common, we get worked up about opposite things.
ameSoeur.q12d: The same things, and for the same reasons.
ameSoeur.q13: Have you been through something difficult together, a loss, an illness, a hard blow?
ameSoeur.q13a: No, never, the relationship is too recent.
ameSoeur.q13d: Yes, several, and we are still here.
ameSoeur.q14: After that hardship, or after your worst argument, the bond was:
ameSoeur.q14a: Damaged. Something did not glue back.
ameSoeur.q14b: Weakened, and we do not talk about it anymore.
ameSoeur.q15: When you argue, how long before you find each other again?
ameSoeur.q15a: Days. Some things never get settled.
ameSoeur.q15b: A long time, and we avoid going back to it.
ameSoeur.q15c: A few hours, we end up talking about it.
ameSoeur.q15d: We repair quickly, and come back to it calmly.
ameSoeur.q16: Has {{name}} ever seen you at your lowest?
ameSoeur.q16a: No, I make sure that never happens.
ameSoeur.q16b: Once, and I was ashamed of it.
ameSoeur.q16d: Yes, several times, and that is when they show up most.
ameSoeur.q17: When you are wrong, can you say so?
ameSoeur.q17a: Never, it turns into a standoff.
ameSoeur.q17b: With difficulty, and often too late.
ameSoeur.q17c: Yes, once I have come back down.
ameSoeur.q18: If your life turned upside down tomorrow, a health problem, a financial blow:
ameSoeur.q18b: I do not know what they would do.
ameSoeur.q18c: I think they would be there.
ameSoeur.q18d: I am certain of it. It is not even a question.
ameSoeur.q19: Your own friends, since you have been with {{name}}:
ameSoeur.q19c: A little less, but they are around.
ameSoeur.q19d: As much as before, and they encourage me to see them.
ameSoeur.q20a: Unthinkable, one of us would take it badly.
ameSoeur.q20d: No problem, and we tell each other everything afterwards.
ameSoeur.q21: Your personal projects, a course, a sport, a wish that does not include {{name}}:
ameSoeur.q21d: They still exist, and {{name}} takes them seriously.
ameSoeur.q22: Since you have been together, you have become:
ameSoeur.q22a: Someone I do not always recognise.
ameSoeur.q22c: More or less the same person.
ameSoeur.q23: When {{name}} is unreachable for a few hours:
ameSoeur.q23a: I cannot manage to do anything else.
ameSoeur.q23c: I think about it, then move on.
ameSoeur.q23d: I get on with my day, simply.
ameSoeur.q24: If this relationship ended, you would still have:
ameSoeur.q24a: Nothing. My whole life revolves around it.
ameSoeur.q24b: Not much to hold on to.
ameSoeur.q24c: A life to rebuild, but some footholds.
ameSoeur.q24d: A life of my own, bruised but standing.
